feasibility_verdict.reason: The architecture family (RMSNorm + RoPE + GQA + SwiGLU, tied embeddings) scales to 100M/300M/1B by changing width/depth/ffn only. No module family change is required. Existing checkpoints cannot warmstart the scaled models (all weights change shape) but the tokenizer is fully reusable.
architecture_risk_items: RoPE beyond 2048 context unvalidated — validated only to 2048
GQA ratio 2:1 retained at all three scales; nothing else changes
vocab 5,822 is small; output projection stays tied and cheap

register_summary.policy: No candidate may enter training merely because it is publicly accessible; every candidate above requires legal sign-off before acquisition or ingestion.

training_strategy.selection_context: L0.1-L0.4 measured: tokenizer adequate; 28.8M model; 20M-token licensed corpus available but 96% general text; frozen benchmark 0/30 for all checkpoints.

strategies.name: Continued pretraining (code-dense)
strategies.description: Warmstart from runs/l03_pretrain/checkpoint_last.pt and continue on a code-dense corpus (L0.4: 50.0% code, 3.18M train tokens).
measured_evidence: L0.3 warmstart run: train loss 8.40 -> 5.05 over 600 steps (1.23M tokens); code-val loss 6.87 -> 5.41 (ppl 967 -> 224).
L0.4 E1 warmstart: code-val loss 5.84 -> 5.34 over 300 steps; E2 code-only 5.62 -> 5.06; E3 (half LR) 5.51.
Every L0.4 checkpoint still scores 0/30 on the frozen Python benchmark.

requirements.unique_data: >= 10-50x the current 1.59M qualified code tokens to begin transferring; 1B-class would need ~100B tokens (off the table)

advantages: cheapest capability path per dollar of new data
monitored divergence (val loss) gives an early stopping signal
limitations: retains English-dominant gravity: without code mass, gains stay numerical (perplexity), not functional
no behavioral alignment: still cannot follow instructions or stop
diminishing returns per epoch; ~4 epochs is a practical ceiling on 17k-line subsets
risks: same English-dominance failure mode as L0.3 revisited at larger scale
license-filtered pool too small to reach useful perplexity scales
unknowns: transfer curve beyond ~2M code tokens (not measurable in this environment)
strategies.verdict: CONTINUE ONLY WITH NEW LICENSED DATA AT SCALE; not a fix in isolation

strategies.name: Code-focused supervised fine-tuning only
strategies.description: SFT on high-quality instruction->code pairs with tests and explanations (the v160/v180 SFT recipe, scaled).
measured_evidence: L0.2 overfit gate: 24/24 memorization with 260 pairs + 1e-3 lr — proves the pipeline can memorize.
L0.2 hp: 260 pairs at 1e-3, 500 steps: train loss 6.38 -> 0.39, code-val loss 4.03 -> ?; still 0/30 unseen.
L0.2 SFT runs systematically degrade code modeling (v180 code val 7.60 vs base 7.43; l02_sft_hp code val 12.31 — catastrophic forgetting of even the tiny base ability).
SFT data with expression-only targets (v1.6/v1.8.0) taught expression-fragment completions and destroyed stopping behavior.

requirements.unique_data: >= 100k-1M high-quality instruction pairs (with tests where feasible) to beat chance on unseen tasks; we have 260 (+ 610 license-verified instruct_v1)
requirements.quality: task descriptions, correct Python solutions, test cases, explanations or code-only targets; multi-step and debugging examples
requirements.provenance: hand-written or license-verified; no LLM-generated pairs (project policy); no benchmark-derived pairs

advantages: most direct route to instruction following and EOS behaviour
each example can be executed and its answer verified before training
limitations: does NOT teach Python itself; only the instruction->code mapping
quality-per-example dominates volume; 57-260 examples cannot beat 0/30
memorization masquerades as capability (24/24 gate fooled nobody on unseen tasks)
risks: catastrophic forgetting of the (already tiny) code-modeling ability
SFT distribution shift can actively worsen held-out code loss, as measured
unknowns: the pair volume at which SFT alone yields nonzero pass@1 for this 28.8M base (untested; expected: far beyond available data)
strategies.verdict: NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT; without a strengthened base it produces memorization, not capability

strategies.name: Combined: continued pretraining + code-focused SFT (two-phase)
strategies.description: Phase 1 continued code-dense pretraining (A), then Phase 2 code-focused SFT (B).
measured_evidence: Phase 1 works: L0.3/L0.4 show monotone code-val improvement (5.96 -> 5.06) with finite gradients and stable clipping.
Phase 2 works mechanically: L0.2 shows pipelines execute, verify, and save cleanly.
No combination attempted yet can be expected to exceed 0/30: each phase is individually data-starved by ~100x.

requirements.phase1: >= 10B tokens of licence-verified code for a 100M-300M model; or accept sub-1B target with smaller but still enormous pool
requirements.compute: phase 1 ~ GPU-hours-to-days depending on size; phase 2 ~ CPU-days once base exists

advantages: aligns with how working code models are actually built (pretrain+anneal+SFT)
both phases are measurable independently (val loss; pass@1 on a frozen benchmark)
limitations: still wholly gated by licensed code at scale; phase 1 cannot be substituted by cleverness
SFT on a weak base cannot raise pass@1; phase order matters
risks: SFT after continued PT could still erase the phase-1 gains if data licensing forces a tiny phase-2 set
unknowns: interaction term between phase-1 volume and phase-2 pair quality for a from-scratch 100M model (no data, no measurement possible here)
strategies.verdict: THE VIABLE ROUTE; both phases required; both blocked on licensed data + compute authorization

strategies.name: Architecture redesign (larger model vs. changes)
strategies.description: Scale up width/depth within the existing Taksh family; or change modules (attention, norm, positional encoding).
measured_evidence: Architecture is NOT the measured bottleneck: perplexity falls monotonically with code-dense training; failures are data-starvation, not attention/norm/rope.
Mechanically verified: RMSNorm+RoPE+GQA+SwiGLU+tied-embedding counts exactly (28,787,328 analytic == measured) and trains stably (grad norms 0.7-2.9).
RoPE validated only to 2048 context; no evidence any module-level change would help at this scale.

requirements.if_scaling: 100M-300M configuration with identical module family (candidate A/B); vocab unchanged
requirements.if_redesign: a measured failure that module changes would fix — none identified; any redesign is speculative

advantages: zero architecture-risk: same family scales cleanly to A/B/C
limitations: redesign without evidence adds unquantifiable risk and zero measured benefit
larger models REQUIRE more data; scaling alone with 1.59M code tokens accelerates memorization
risks: C_1B without a matched data increase is wasted memory, not capability
unknowns: ablations (e.g. different GQA ratio, finer token granularity) untested; all blocked on data anyway
strategies.verdict: DO NOT REDESIGN; scale with data. Consider A/B only after data authorization

training_strategy.recommendation: Sequence: (1) owner authorizes data acquisition + legal review (candidate corpora in the register); (2) A100-class compute; (3) strategy C: continued pretraining at 100M, then code-focused SFT; (4) re-run the frozen L0.2 benchmark with the identical protocol; (5) keep the L0.1 default checkpoint until a candidate demonstrably beats it on the frozen benchmark.
do_not: do not switch the L0.1 default checkpoint
do not train on L0.2 benchmark items or derivatives
do not scale the model beyond data scale

method.flops: training FLOPs = 6 x parameters x training tokens (standard forward+backward approximation)
limitations: attention-quadratic term ignored (valid for d_model <= 2048, seq <= 2048-4096)
activation memory is a rule-of-thumb (34 x bsz x seq x d x layers), not a profiler measurement
GPU durations carry no utilization claim; only CPU duration is anchored to measurement
assumptions: fp32 or bf16 mixed precision; ~16 bytes/parameter working set either way

bar_for_claiming_coding_capability.functional_correctness: >= 15/30 problems (>= 50%) functionally correct with zero benchmark-set leakage

bar_for_claiming_coding_capability.repeat_consistency: 100% byte-identical greedy completions across repeated runs on all 30 problems

bar_for_claiming_coding_capability.benchmark_integrity: frozen hash unchanged; no training item shares an instruction/entry-point with the bench

current_measured_state.functional_correctness: 0/30 for every checkpoint tested this campaign
current_measured_state.verdict_vs_bar: every bar fails; capability NOT demonstrated by any checkpoint

acceptance_criteria_definition.note: Criteria are fixed and not lowered. A lower perplexity or a fluent response does not count.

decision.reason: A technically credible route exists (architecture scales; tokenizer is adequate; pipeline is built and verified; license-qualified data paths exist), but capability is demonstrated nowhere yet: 0/30 on the frozen benchmark for every checkpoint tested, and the qualified code supply (1.59M tokens) is ~100x below the minimum for the smallest interesting model.
